market_question: Will Dan Cox win the 2026 Maryland Governor Republican primary election?
reasoning: Dan Cox is a far-right Trump ally who lost the 2022 general election by 32 points, making him a weak general-election candidate. Maryland Republican insiders are likely to coalesce around a more moderate, electable challenger to avoid a repeat loss. While Cox retains strong support among the MAGA base that gave him his primary win in 2022, the party apparatus and donor class will likely back an alternative, reducing his chances to around 35%.
evidence_points: Cox lost the 2022 gubernatorial election to Wes Moore by 32 points, raising electability concerns.
Maryland Republican primary voters, while Trump-aligned, may prioritize a candidate with broader appeal for the general election.
Establishment Republican groups and funding will likely consolidate behind a challenger to block Cox.
sources_consulted: History of Maryland Republican primary dynamics
Analysis of Trump's influence in Maryland GOP after 2024
